OK-2026-SB1319.aiSummary: The bill would set up a process for homeowners to ask for help when their home is contaminated by substances like brine or oil that fall under the Corporation Commission’s power. It would create a Remediation Assistance Revolving Fund to pay for cleanup, stopping the contamination, and in some cases buying the property at fair market value. Cities or counties could hold the property, help remove a residence if needed, and return sale money to the fund. The measure was approved by the governor and takes effect as an emergency law.

OK-2026-SB2.aiSummary: The bill would set new distance rules for wind energy projects in Oklahoma. It would require wind towers to be at least one-quarter mile from homes and from nonparticipating property after November 1, 2025, and it would keep other setback rules in place for airports, schools, hospitals, and military sites. It also would require proof of federal aviation review and cleared defense issues to be filed, with daily fines of up to $1,500 for violations.

OK-2026-SB1326.aiSummary: The measure changes rules for self-storage liens and rental agreements in Oklahoma. It lets rental agreements be sent and accepted by email if both sides agree, and it says an occupant’s rent payment or continued use can count as acceptance if the person does not sign within 30 days after the agreement is delivered. It also sets rules for towing vehicles after 60 days of unpaid rent and for notice before stored property can be treated as abandoned. It becomes effective November 1, 2026.
